data_source: synthetic demo scenario 'dry-extreme' — deterministic, offline, generated by core/demo.py
demo_disclaimer: Demo / synthetic scenario — not a live forecast or observation.
hourly_scope: issue day (Day +0) only — the daily table carries the full 5-day outlook

bands.meaning: Thermal stress is within the range most healthy adults tolerate.
Rising thermal stress; heat-sensitive groups should start adapting schedules.
Dangerous thermal stress for outdoor exposure; municipal heat actions should activate.
Life-threatening thermal stress possible; emergency heat-health response.

heat_index_c.formula: NWS Rothfusz regression evaluated in °F with the three standard NWS adjustments (low-RH, high-RH, simple-formula switch below 80 °F); implementation core.thermal.heat_index.
heat_index_c.limitations: Assumes shade and no wind; ignores solar radiation and individual physiology. Public-messaging number, not a risk-model driver.
heat_index_c.valid_range: Designed for air temperature ≥ 26.7 °C (80 °F) and RH 20–100 %. Below 20 °C air temperature is returned unchanged.

utci_c.limitations: NOT COMPUTED. Full UTCI needs mean radiant temperature and its 6th-order polynomial; rather than ship a mislabelled approximation, estimated WBGT is the radiation-aware metric of record.

wbgt_est_c.formula: ISO 7243 outdoor WBGT = 0.7·Tw + 0.2·Tg + 0.1·Ta when shortwave > 20 W/m², else shade form 0.7·Tw + 0.3·Ta. Tg from a 150 mm black-globe energy balance with Ranz–Marshall convection (Nu = 2 + 0.6·Re^0.5·Pr^⅓) and linearised radiation; absorptivity 0.95.
wbgt_est_c.limitations: ESTIMATED WBGT — no physical globe thermometer is involved. Assumes standard globe geometry and pressure; cloud/radiation come from the same forecast as temperature, so errors are correlated.
wbgt_est_c.valid_range: Outdoor conditions representable by forecast T/RH/wind/radiation; Tw via Stull's envelope.

wet_bulb_c.formula: Stull (2011) empirical natural wet-bulb from T and RH at standard pressure; validated in-repo against a psychrometric inversion (max deviation ≈ 0.55 °C, RH ≥ 50 % regime).
wet_bulb_c.limitations: Empirical fit, not a psychrometric measurement.

estimated.meaning: Computed from model/forecast inputs (temperature, humidity, wind, shortwave radiation) with the documented formula. All required inputs were present. This is NOT a globe-thermometer measurement.

measured.meaning: Observed by a physical instrument at the location.

partial-input.meaning: Computed with at least one required input missing and replaced by the documented assumption listed in `assumptions`. Treat as lower-confidence than `estimated`.

unavailable.meaning: A mandatory input (air temperature or relative humidity) is missing. No value is produced — we never invent one.

method.score_formula: HTSI = 100 · clip((WBGT_est − 25) / (36 − 25), 0, 1)^1.4 + min(8, 1.6 · max(0, Tmax − Tmax_normal(1991–2020))) when a fixed climate normal is available; clipped to 0–100. The anomaly term represents acclimatisation stress: heat further above the local normal harms more at the same absolute WBGT.
method.separation_rule: Meteorological stress only. Vulnerability and demographics are NOT inputs to this index; they are combined separately and transparently in the health-impact indicator (core/health_impact.py).

scenario.data_source: synthetic demo scenario 'dry-extreme' — deterministic, offline, generated by core/demo.py
scenario.demo_disclaimer: Demo / synthetic scenario — not a live forecast or observation.
scenario.issued_at_note: Fixed scenario timestamp (intentional): the demo clock never moves, so 'Day +3' is always 2026-05-21 regardless of when you open the demo.
scenario.label: Dry extreme heatwave — severe at lead 3–5
scenario.summary: A dry heat dome builds over the region. Tmax climbs from 43 °C on the issue day to 47.6 °C by Day +4 — departures of +6 to +7.4 °C over the fixed 1991–2020 normal. Days +2 to +5 form a declared SEVERE heatwave episode (≥2-day persistence), so warnings carry real lead time of 3, 4 and 5 days.
teaching_points: Lead times 3/4/5 days on a declared episode — the product's core promise
Two-day persistence rule: the first candidate day stays an early watch
Dry air keeps wet-bulb/WBGT far below the Heat Index — the metrics disagree because they answer different questions

wbgt_statement: wbgt_est_c is an ESTIMATED WBGT computed from scenario weather inputs with the ISO 7243 outdoor formula. It is not a measured globe-thermometer WBGT and must never be labelled as one.
